name: ExamesIA (examesia.com.br)
category: AI lab-exam interpreter / clinical decision support SaaS for health professionals (upload-PDF-interpretation category); NOT a lab, NOT patient-facing
stage: Early-stage / stealth-launch startup. Solo founder (Dr. Rafael Mustafa, physician, also listed as DPO). Site is a 6-page Next.js app on Vercel; terms/privacy versioned 2026-07; domain registered 2023-01-24 (repurposed), DNSSEC enabled 2026-06-19, Vercel deployment fresh. No press, no Product Hunt, no LinkedIn company page, dead Instagram handle, empty GitHub org. Distinct older namesake examesia.com (patient-facing, free) is defunct — domain now redirects to an e-book marketplace. [uncertain]
pricing_model: Freemium trial + professional subscriptions (Stripe). Free: 7 days / 20 readings, no card. Basic R$47.90/month (40 readings); Pro R$99.90/month (100 readings, patient-ready report, priority support, 'most popular'); Max R$199.90/month (290 readings, team volume, discounted credit packs). Overage via standalone credit packs ('creditos avulsos'). Claimed unit economics on landing: ~R$0.12 average cost per reading. Cancel anytime. No recent price changes observed (short lifetime).
target_user: Health professionals who read exams daily: recently graduated doctors (confidence), ER/on-call physicians (speed), nutrologists (weight loss), clinical and sports nutritionists, endocrinologists and performance/hormonal-lifestyle medicine. Explicitly B2B (professional tool), not lay patients.
scale_metrics: No public user, revenue, funding, or valuation numbers; no funding signals (bootstrap/solo). Web footprint near zero: ~9 DuckDuckGo results, no press coverage, no app store presence, no testimonials on landing. Assessment: noise, not a durable threat today — but a live, monetized entrant validating professional willingness-to-pay in the category. [uncertain]
core_features: Upload exam as PDF or photo from any lab; AI auto-extracts all markers (no manual entry); abnormal values highlighted against reference ranges (e.g. example shows 16 flagged markers with refs); markers grouped by body system (glycemic-metabolic, hormonal, vitamins, renal, etc.); per-system probable diagnosis ('Dx provavel', e.g. insulin resistance via HOMA-IR 3.78) + conduct to validate + supplementation suggestions (e.g. vitamin D with K2, dose ranges as 'educational reference'); automatic patient evolution comparison across exam dates; patient-ready report generation (Pro plan and up); reading quota + credit-pack metering; auth via email/Google/magic link.
signature_differentiator: Sells pre-packaged clinical reasoning, not just extraction: for each system the AI outputs probable differential diagnosis + next steps to validate + supplementation protocol, with the professional as validator ('A IA sugere, voce revisa e valida. A conduta e sempre sua'). Positioning is openly anti-generic-ChatGPT for the consultorio: copy-paste-free reading, persistent patient history, LGPD/CFM compliance framing, and a cost-per-reading price anchor (R$0.12). Because the user is a clinician, it dares to state 'probable diagnosis' — a claim patient-facing rivals (including Dr. Exame) deliberately avoid.
lab_data_handling: Any laboratory, upload-only: PDF or photo. LLM-based extraction and interpretation; no lab integrations, no LIS/RNDS connectivity. Interpretation is their own AI layer (Anthropic + OpenAI per privacy policy), reference ranges taken from the report. No retest cadence of their own — follow-up intervals appear inside AI conduct suggestions (e.g. 'reassess in 90 days'), so cadence is clinician-driven. No hardware, no at-home testing, no wearables.
family_dependents_depth: None marketed. The unit is the professional account with patient records; no dependent profiles, no caregiver mode, no pediatric reference ranges, no hereditary-risk features visible anywhere on the site. Complete blind spot (Dr. Exame pillar uncontested here).
doctor_sharing: Inverted model: the doctor IS the user. The shareable artifact is the AI-generated report/laudo 'ready for the patient' (Pro plan). No SOAP note, no consultation-brief workflow, no doctor-patient messaging or portal advertised.
action_loop_monetization: Post-interpretation actions are suggestions only: conduct to validate (diet/exercise, reassess in 90 days) and supplementation protocols (vitamin D+K2, B12) with dose ranges flagged as educational, final dose = professional's decision. No supplement marketplace, no telemedicine, no prescriptions, no imaging/MCED referral loop. Monetization stops at metered readings (subscription + credits); the action loop is open for someone else to capture.
ai_approach: LLM-based via commercial APIs — privacy policy names Anthropic AND OpenAI as subprocessors for exam AI processing; providers contractually do not train on submitted data. No proprietary clinical model, no published accuracy, no model card. Human-in-the-loop is the professional: AI suggests, clinician reviews, edits and validates; terms repeat 'AI can make mistakes' and 'does not issue diagnosis'.
data_inputs: Single input: lab exam files (PDF or image). No wearables, no genetics, no CGM, no questionnaires, no manual entry advertised.
data_interoperability: Narrow: ingest = PDF/image upload; exhaust = patient-ready report. No FHIR, no Health Connect, no Apple Health Records, no RNDS/REL, no LIS integration, no WhatsApp channel. Ingestion breadth is NOT their moat — speed-to-value on a single PDF is.
platform: Web app only (Next.js on Vercel, Supabase for DB/auth incl. Google OAuth and magic link). No native mobile app, no public API, no extension.
onboarding: Friction-light: create account (email, Google, or magic link) -> 7-day free trial with 20 readings, no credit card -> upload PDF -> reading 'in seconds'. Landing promises 3 steps, 'no learning curve', time-to-value = first uploaded exam. Consent banner at signup discloses AI processing for decision support.
data_visualization: Example page shows the output shape: flat alert list of abnormal markers with value + unit + reference range, then system-grouped cards (Glycemic-metabolic, Hormonal, Vitamins, Renal 'no relevant changes') each containing Dx provavel, conduct, and supplementation text. Evolution = automatic cross-date comparison (representation unknown). No charts, no scores, no trend graphs advertised. Text-first layout. [uncertain]
engagement_channel: Nothing visible: no WhatsApp, no email nudges, no community, no streaks; Instagram handle @examesia dead/unavailable, no LinkedIn company page, no content/blog (sitemap = 6 pages). Retention rests on the subscription quota itself (metered readings create sunk-credit psychology). Weakest surface of the product. [uncertain]
clinical_validation_trust: No accuracy claim, no methodology published, no clinical advisory board cited; landing statistics (38% of doctors use generative AI; 64% fear LGPD) are uncredited. Mitigators: consistent 'decision support, does not diagnose, professional validates' framing in terms and on-report disclaimers; exams not used for model training; named DPO (Dr. Rafael Mustafa) with contact; Stripe billing, cancel anytime, liability capped at 12 months of payments. Risk list: 'Dx provavel' wording rides the edge of diagnosis claims; solo-physician operation with gmail DPO contact signals thin governance; zero external validation (no reviews, no press, no case studies).
regulatory_posture: Positioned as a clinical decision support tool for licensed professionals (terms require professional eligibility), which is the classic dodge away from patient-facing SaMD classification under ANVISA RDC 657/2022; no ANVISA registration mentioned anywhere. LGPD posture is unusually crafted: split roles — platform is CONTROLLER only for the professional's account data and OPERATOR for patient data inside exams (professional is controller), international transfer via contractual safeguards, deletion on account closure. Claims compliance with LGPD and 'CFM 2.454' (medical-council norm cited without detail). No FDA posture (Brazil-only). [uncertain]
gaps_opportunities: They do NOT have: any patient-facing surface (Dr. Exame's core), family/dependents/caregiver mode, pediatric ranges, charts/trends/scores, wearable or Health Connect ingestion, WhatsApp retention channel, lab/LIS/RNDS integrations, telemedicine/prescription/supplement action loop, mobile app, social proof, brand strength (collides with defunct examesia.com). Opportunities for Dr. Exame: (1) their existence prices the PRO side of the category at R$47.90-199.90/month — validates selling to doctors directly, where Dr. Exame already has a free mirror-portal wedge; (2) patient-side interpretation + doctor validation is a superset they cannot reach without pivoting; (3) their text-only, chartless output and dead social presence leave UX and trust differentiation open. Worth copying (inspiration, not verbatim): per-system grouping with dx+conduct packaging; controller/operator LGPD framing for shared exam data; cost-per-reading anchor in pricing communication; nutritionists as a paying segment adjacent to doctors.
relevance: Medium. Same category and same motion (Brazil, upload PDF, AI interpretation, lightweight), and it monetizes the professional side of the same workflow Dr. Exame's doctor portal serves for free — a direct-ish competitor if it grows. But: zero traction signals, solo founder, no patient surface, no engagement loop, and brand collision with a dead namesake. Today it is validation of market demand more than a threat.
